module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Diam
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Metric

@[expose] public section

assert_not_exists Field

namespace SimpleGraph
variable {α : Type*} {G G' : SimpleGraph α}

/--
The diameter is the greatest distance between any two vertices. If the graph is disconnected,
this will be `0`.
-/
lemma diam_eq_zero_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton α] : G.diam = 0 := by
  simp [diam, ediam_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton.mpr (by assumption)]

proof_wanted diam_ne_zero [Nontrivial α] : G.diam ≠ 0

lemma nontrivial_of_diam_ne_zero' (h : G.diam ≠ 0) : Nontrivial α := by
  contrapose! h
  exact diam_eq_zero_of_subsingleton

section Path
open Path

proof_wanted dist_le_diam_of_mem_path {G : SimpleGraph α} {u v : α} (p : G.Walk u v) (w : α)
    (hw : w ∈ p.support) : G.dist w u ≤ G.diam

end Path

end SimpleGraph

findings.description: The proof request at DiamExtra.lean:35 assumes only `[Nontrivial α]`, but natural-valued diameter can be zero on a nontrivial graph. Take `α = Fin 2` and `G = ⊥`: the hypothesis holds, while `SimpleGraph.diam_bot` gives `G.diam = 0`. This counterexample was checked in Lean. The missing condition is finite extended diameter, not merely nontriviality or connectivity; a connected infinite ray also has natural-valued diameter zero.
findings.source_evidence: The imported Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Diam.lean:261–266 defines `diam := G.ediam.toNat` and explicitly gives it value zero when distances are unbounded or the graph is disconnected. Its correct positivity lemma, `diam_ne_zero_of_ediam_ne_top` (line 297), requires both `[Nontrivial α]` and `G.ediam ≠ ⊤`.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove this request in favor of the imported `SimpleGraph.diam_ne_zero_of_ediam_ne_top`, or add `(h : G.ediam ≠ ⊤)` and prove it using that lemma. Alternatively, `[Finite α]` together with `G.Connected` suffices. The unconditional extended-diameter version is already `SimpleGraph.ediam_ne_zero`.

findings.description: The proof request at DiamExtra.lean:44–45 treats membership in one walk as sufficient for a bound by the whole graph's natural-valued diameter. On `Fin 3`, let the only edge be 0–1 and let vertex 2 be isolated. For the one-edge path `p : G.Walk 0 1` and `w = 1`, membership holds and `G.dist 1 0 = 1`, but `G.diam = 0` because the graph is disconnected. The requested inequality is therefore `1 ≤ 0`. Lean verified this counterexample, including that `p.IsPath`; replacing `Walk` with `Path` would not repair it.
findings.source_evidence: Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Diam.lean:271 states `dist_le_diam (h : G.ediam ≠ ⊤)`, while line 278 gives zero natural-valued diameter for disconnected graphs. Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Metric.lean:308 states that adjacent vertices have distance one. Walk membership ensures local reachability, not finite extended diameter of the entire graph.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `(h : G.ediam ≠ ⊤)`; the conclusion then follows immediately from `SimpleGraph.dist_le_diam h`, without using the walk assumptions. Alternatively, state the unconditional extended-valued bound `G.edist w u ≤ G.ediam`, already provided by `SimpleGraph.edist_le_ediam`. Connectivity alone is insufficient without a boundedness or finiteness assumption.

findings.description: The proved lemma at DiamExtra.lean:37 exactly duplicates the already imported Mathlib lemma `SimpleGraph.nontrivial_of_diam_ne_zero`: both have the same vertex-type and graph parameters and conclude `Nontrivial α` from `G.diam ≠ 0`. Its mathematics is correct; this is duplicate library API.
findings.source_evidence: Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Diam.lean:274–276 already proves `lemma nontrivial_of_diam_ne_zero (h : G.diam ≠ 0) : Nontrivial α`. The matching types were confirmed with Lean.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the primed duplicate and use `SimpleGraph.nontrivial_of_diam_ne_zero`.
